statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 8 (low) sits well below the block threshold as NQ retraces 171 points off the 29,274.75 overnight low and holds it for a sixth hour, while Stress 40 (moderate) reflects Brent above $90, September rate-hike odds near 60% after the Jackson Hole remarks, and a month-end session that runs into payrolls week.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers 13:30-14:30 UTC, where the U.S. cash open on the final August session meets month-end rebalancing and the first deep-liquidity pricing of both the weekend Iran escalation and the hawkish Fed repricing. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100: the overnight shock keeps retracing as NQ recovers to -0.16%, while $90 Brent and hawkish Fed repricing hold Stress up
body: The retracement that began overnight has extended. The Nasdaq-100 September contract trades 29,446.00, down 45.75 points or 0.16% against Friday's 29,491.75 settlement, inside an unchanged overnight range of 29,274.75 to 29,545.50. That low, printed around the 00:00 UTC hour after Iran answered the U.S. strike on two rocket launchers at Larak Island with missiles at U.S. forces in Jordan, has now held about five and a half hours, and price has recovered roughly 171 points from it. Asian cash markets show the same shape: the Nikkei 225 is 66,113.49, down 0.44%, after trading as low as 64,832.10. This is orderly two-way price discovery with genuine retracement, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement path that the tail measure is built to detect, so Tail eases from 10 to 8. The stress backdrop is unchanged and remains real. Brent is $90.51, up 2.74%, and WTI $85.52, up 2.54%, carrying a geopolitical premium after the Larak Island strike, with Kharg Island still idle under the naval blockade and the reported claim of a fresh attack there uncorroborated. The rates picture is the second driver: after the hawkish Jackson Hole remarks from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, futures markets price roughly a 60% chance of a September rate increase against about 35% beforehand, and the 10-year yield sits near 4.71%. The 2-year at 4.327% is 2.3 basis points lower on the day, a small easing at the front end that does not undo Friday's repricing. Cross-asset alignment is therefore incomplete: equities are retracing higher while oil is bid and yields are broadly steady, which supports Stress at 40 rather than an increase in Tail. The shared Finviz context file is roughly 230 minutes old, past its 90-minute freshness limit, so it was treated as stale and excluded from the evidence base; all levels above come from independent primary-source research. Confidence is 88 on a current futures quote, a live Asian cash reference, current oil and 2-year yield prints and verified reporting on both the Fed and the Gulf. The day ahead carries month-end rebalancing on the final August session, the Dallas Fed Manufacturing Index at 14:30 UTC, and a UK market closed for the Summer Bank Holiday that will thin European liquidity.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment, spanning the closed Sunday market, the CME weekly reopen and the first hours of the new session. The first seventeen of those hours sat inside the weekend halt with Tail fixed at the floor of 5, dominant mode normal and status green, while Stress drifted from 25 to 32 as the reopen approached and Confidence rebuilt from 64 to 87 as primary sources were re-verified each hour. The 22:00 UTC reopen lifted Tail to 9, and the Larak Island strike and the Iranian missile response pushed the peak to 15 with Stress 44 and dominant mode trend-down in the 00:00 UTC hour, the only trend-down reading of the window. Every hour since has retraced: Tail 13, 11, 10 and 10 with dominant mode mixed, tracking the recovery in NQ and in Asian cash indices. Status was green and the mapped action EA_ON in all 24 slots, and no hour reached the 25 block threshold.
outlookSummary: The current hour records a shock that is not merely absorbed but actively retracing: NQ 29,446.00, down 0.16%, the 29,274.75 low intact about five and a half hours and 171 points below the market, and the Nikkei recovered roughly 1,281 points off its own low. Tail therefore eases to 8 with Stress 40 and Confidence 88. The conditional path holds at 8 to 9 through a European session thinned by the London Summer Bank Holiday, builds through the U.S. pre-market to a conditional peak of 15 in the hour that spans the cash-open aftermath and the 14:30 UTC Dallas Fed release, then decays into the afternoon. A second, smaller conditional rise to 13 covers the month-end closing auction on the last August session, where index rebalancing can concentrate a one-directional imbalance with a fixed end time. The CME maintenance break takes conditional Tail to its 7 trough, after which the 1 September Asian session is carried at 9 to 10 with Confidence decaying from 71 to 65 with distance from verified evidence. No forecast hour reaches the 25 block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON across all 24 slots. The published danger window stays narrow at 13:30 to 14:30 UTC.
